name: token-field
title: TokenField
description: Text with tokens inside it — a notification target, an alert's audience.

files.content: import { createContext, useContext } from 'react' import { Button as AriaButton, Label as AriaLabel, Tag as AriaTag, TagGroup as AriaTagGroup, TagList as AriaTagList, } from 'react-aria-components' import type { LabelProps as AriaLabelProps, TagGroupProps as AriaTagGroupProps, TagListProps as AriaTagListProps, TagProps as AriaTagProps, } from 'react-aria-components' import { LABEL } from '../field' /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag`: a 12px uppercase chip with a transparent 1px edge, so every variant is the * same box however it is filled. * * **The hover state is `:hover`, not `data-hovered`.** React Aria's `Tag` does not provide one — * a real pointer hover leaves the tag without the attribute, which this component's own test caught. * Everywhere else in this system `data-[hovered]` is right because React Aria supplies it; here the * only honest source of "the pointer is on this chip" is the browser's own pseudo-class. * * The hover recipe is the same one the button uses — the tag's own colour deepened toward ink — and * for the same reason. The sheet brightens its chips with `filter: brightness(1.08)`, which is * invisible on a fill that already sits near the top of its range and says nothing at all about * *which* tag you are pointing at. `--tag-hover` is declared by each variant and read here, so the * recipe and the base land on the same element. */ export const CHIP = [ 'inline-flex items-center', 'border px-2.5 py-1', 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.01em] uppercase', 'transition-[color,background-color,border-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse', ].join(' ') export const TAG_CHIP = [ CHIP, 'cursor-pointer', 'hover:bg-(--tag-hover)', 'data-[pressed]:bg-(--tag-pressed)', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-1 data-[focus-visible]:outline-offset-2', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-ring', 'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40', // A tag with a remove button is still one chip, so the button sits inside the box rather than // beside it. '[&[data-rac]]:select-none', ].join(' ') /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag--*`, one per variant it defines — seven, because that is how many it has. * * `default` and `outline` are the two outlines, and `outline` is the one the sheet gives the accent * on hover. The three fills carry `ink`. The two accented outlines take a wash of their own colour, * which is the same "derive from the base" rule the fills follow — an outline has no fill to deepen, * so it gains one. * * Every one of these is written out in full rather than built from a template string: Tailwind reads * source text, and `var(--color-${token})` is not source text it can see. */ const VARIANT: Record = { default: 'border-transparent text-foreground/70 hover:text-foreground', outline: 'border-input text-foreground/70 hover:border-primary hover:text-primary', teal: '[--tag:var(--color-primary)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', gray: '[--tag:var(--color-secondary)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-secondary)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-secondary)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', yellow: '[--tag:var(--color-warning)] [--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_88%,var(--color-ink))] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_78%,var(--color-ink))] border-transparent bg-(--tag) text-ink', 'outline-ring': '[--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_14%,transparent)] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-primary)_22%,transparent)] border-primary text-primary', 'outline-warning': '[--tag-hover:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_14%,transparent)] [--tag-pressed:color-mix(in_oklch,var(--color-warning)_22%,transparent)] border-warning text-warning', } export type TagVariant = | 'default' | 'outline' | 'teal' | 'gray' | 'yellow' | 'outline-ring' | 'outline-warning' /** * The label inside a tag, and the anchor it becomes when the tag has an `href`. React Aria reports a * tag with an `href` as `data-href` on a grid row and renders no anchor itself — the same as its * navigation tree — so the destination is drawn here. A tag is a real link or it is a chip, and * `middle-click`, "open in a new tab" and the status bar all need the anchor. */ const LINK = 'inline-flex min-w-0 items-center text-inherit no-underline' const HREF = createContext(undefined) /** * The remove button, drawn when the group allows removing. React Aria marks the tag * `data-allows-removing` and leaves the control to the consumer, exactly as it does for the tree's * disclosure — so this writes it, for the same reason `Table.Selection` writes its own slot: the one * attribute that makes it work is the one nobody remembers. */ export const TAG_REMOVE = [ 'ms-1.5 -me-1 grid size-3.5 shrink-0 cursor-pointer place-items-center', 'text-current opacity-55', 'transition-opacity duration-[120ms] ease-pulse', 'hover:opacity-100', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-1 data-[focus-visible]:outline-offset-1', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-current', ].join(' ') /** The list wraps, because chips that overflow a column are the one thing a tag group is for. */ const LIST = 'flex flex-wrap gap-2' // Not generic, unlike `TagListProps`: React Aria's own `TagGroupProps` is not — a tag group's items // are tags, and the group itself owns no data of its own. export interface TagGroupProps extends Omit< AriaTagGroupProps, | 'children' | 'className' | 'selectionMode' | 'selectedKeys' | 'defaultSelectedKeys' | 'onSelectionChange' | 'disabledKeys' | 'onRemove' > { /** `none`, `single` or `multiple`. */ selectionMode?: AriaTagGroupProps['selectionMode'] /** The chosen chips, by each tag's `id`. */ selectedKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['selectedKeys'] /** What starts chosen. */ defaultSelectedKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['defaultSelectedKeys'] /** Called with the new set of keys. */ onSelectionChange?: AriaTagGroupProps['onSelectionChange'] /** Chips that cannot be chosen. */ disabledKeys?: AriaTagGroupProps['disabledKeys'] /** Called when a chip's remove button is pressed. */ onRemove?: AriaTagGroupProps['onRemove'] /** `className` places the group; the chips' own styling stays internal. */ className?: string /** A `TagGroup.Label`, then a `TagGroup.List`. */ children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagGroupLabelProps extends AriaLabelProps { children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagGroupListProps extends Omit< AriaTagListProps, 'className' > { className?: string children?: React.ReactNode } export interface TagProps extends Omit { /** Which of the sheet's chips this is. */ variant?: TagVariant /** * Turns the chip into a link. React Aria matches it, and this component draws the anchor — a tag * with an `href` is a grid row with `data-href` and nothing to click otherwise. */ href?: string className?: string children?: React.ReactNode } /** * The group's legend. Use it as `TagGroup.Label`, above a `TagGroup.List`. * * Exported as `TagGroupLabel` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form * `TagGroup.Label`. */ export function TagGroupLabel({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupLabelProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * The chips. Use it as `TagGroup.List`, wrapping the `TagGroup.Tag`s. * * Exported as `TagGroupList` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form * `TagGroup.List`. */ export function TagGroupList({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupListProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * One chip. Use it as `TagGroup.Tag`. Give it an `href` and it is a link rather than a value — the * sheet uses its tags both ways, which is why `Tag` takes `LinkDOMProps`. * * Exported as `TagItem` only so tooling can resolve it; consume the compound form `TagGroup.Tag`. */ export function TagItem({ variant = 'default', href, className, children, ...props }: TagProps) { const inherited = useContext(HREF) const target = href ?? inherited return ( {({ allowsRemoving }) => ( <> {target ? ( // A link needs a wrapper, and a wrapper makes the children "non-plain text" — which is // React Aria's cue to ask for `textValue`, because it can no longer read the name off // the markup. A chip with no destination keeps its text bare and needs nothing. {children} ) : ( children )} {allowsRemoving ? ( ) : null} )} ) } /** * Styled element. Not exported — `TagGroup` below is the public symbol, and docgen reads the JSDoc * from the *exported* declaration, not this one. */ function TagGroupRoot({ className, children, ...props }: TagGroupProps) { return ( {children} ) } /** * The sheet's `.ds-tag`: a 12px uppercase chip, in the seven treatments the sheet defines. * * ```tsx * * * fra1 * iad1 * sfo1 * * * ``` * * Add `selectionMode="multiple"` and the chips become selectable rather than decorative, add a * `href` and they become links — the sheet uses them all three ways, and React Aria decides which * one it is from the props rather than from a different component. * * ### A tag is not a button * * It is a short piece of metadata with an edge. The moment it carries an action, it is a button and * should look like one; the moment it carries nothing but a value, it does not need to be a control * at all. `selectionMode` says the chips are chosen; without it they are labels, and adding * `onRemove` to a group that was never selectable makes a control out of decoration. * * ### Hover deepens the tag's own colour, rather than brightening it * * The sheet's `a.ds-tag:hover { filter: brightness(1.08) }` cannot survive five fills: on a * near-white yellow it is invisible, and on any of them it says nothing about which tag the pointer * is on. Fills deepen toward `--color-ink` — the recipe the button uses — and the two accented * outlines, which have no fill to deepen, take a wash of their own colour instead. Both derive from * the base; neither substitutes a different one. * * The `outline` variant's edge is `--input` rather than the sheet's 35% white, which * measures under the 3:1 a boundary needs on the dark page. It is the same correction the rest of * the system makes, and the reason `--input` exists. */ export const TagGroup = Object.assign(TagGroupRoot, { Label: TagGroupLabel, List: TagGroupList, Tag: TagItem, })

/**
 * The field anatomy, shared by every control that wears it — `TextField`,
 * `SearchField`, and the textarea, select, checkbox and radio still to come.
 *
 * Only the styling lives here. Each component defines its own slot components,
 * thin as they are, so that its docs and manifest describe its own API rather
 * than pointing at another component's.
 */

/**
 * The three control sizes. `size` is set once on the field and travels as two
 * custom properties rather than through React context: the control, and any
 * affix inside it, are ordinary descendants of the field, so inheritance already
 * does the work. It also means a one-off override is just a utility on the
 * element rather than a new prop.
 */
export type FieldSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

export const FIELD_SIZES: Record<FieldSize, string> = {
  sm: '[--field-control-h:2.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.8125rem]', // 36px / 13px
  md: '[--field-control-h:2.75rem] [--field-control-text:0.875rem]', // 44px / 14px
  lg: '[--field-control-h:3.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.9375rem]', // 52px / 15px
}

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field`: legend, control, then the hint that explains it.
 *
 * The `font-size` here is what the control and any affix inherit. It sits on the
 * field rather than on the input so it still reaches an affix, which is the
 * input's sibling — a `cap`-sized icon would otherwise match the page's font
 * instead of the field's.
 *
 * The two border properties are published here for the same reason `Checkbox`
 * publishes its own: read-only lives on the field root, while the border it changes
 * is on the input, and a group variant cannot win that cascade — see the note on
 * `INPUT`. Declaring them here means the input only reads them, and the ordinary
 * cascade decides, because `[data-readonly]` plainly outranks the bare declaration.
 */
export const FIELD = [
  'group flex flex-col gap-2 [font-size:var(--field-control-text)]',
  '[--field-border:var(--color-input)]',
  '[--field-hover:var(--color-border)]',
  // Read-only is not disabled: the value is the whole point of the field, so it
  // keeps full-strength text. Only the affordances go — a quieter hairline, and no
  // brightening on hover — because there is nothing here to invite a click on.
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-border:var(--color-border-soft)]',
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-hover:var(--color-border-soft)]',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix` wrapper. `Group` exists for one case: an affix is
 * positioned against the control, but the field also holds the legend and the
 * hint, so an affix anchored to the field would centre on all three.
 * Wrapping the control gives the affix the right box — and it stays opt-in, so a
 * plain field has no extra element at all.
 *
 * The two `:has()` rules are here for the same reason: the room an affix needs is
 * padding on the input, and the group is what can see both of them. The input
 * itself never has to know it has neighbours.
 */
export const GROUP = [
  'relative flex w-full',
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-start]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:ps-10.5', // 42px, per the sheet's search field
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-end]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:pe-14', // 56px, per the sheet's trailing unit
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`: 12px, uppercase, letterspaced, white 70%.
 *
 * The required marker is drawn from the field's own `data-required`, so the label
 * never has to be told and the asterisk cannot drift out of sync with
 * `isRequired`. The input already carries the native `required`, so this is the
 * visual half of the same fact.
 */
export const LABEL = [
  'text-[12px] uppercase tracking-[0.04em] text-muted-foreground',
  "group-data-[required]:after:ms-1 group-data-[required]:after:text-destructive group-data-[required]:after:content-['*']",
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-input`.
 *
 * The resting hairline is what identifies the control. The sheet gives
 * `.ds-input` a transparent border and leaves the panel-2 fill to do the job, but
 * that fill is 1.23:1 on the dark page and 1.17:1 on the light one, so the field is
 * nearly invisible as a boundary in both. `--input` is the smallest
 * hairline that clears the 3:1 a control boundary needs on each.
 *
 * Hover has to *strengthen* it rather than replace it: the sheet's hover is white
 * at 25%, which is now weaker than the resting line and would erase it.
 *
 * `outline-none` on focus suppresses the *browser's* ring, which is what the
 * sheet's `.ds-input:focus { outline: none }` is really doing. Chrome gives a
 * focused text input its `:focus-visible` ring at `outline-style: auto` regardless
 * of React Aria's attribute, so leaving it alone means a blue UA ring on a teal
 * system. Focus is then the border alone — adding the shared 3px-offset ring here
 * would draw two parallel teal hairlines with a gap, which reads as a fault.
 * `Button` can carry that ring because the edge it repeats is a solid fill.
 */
export const INPUT = [
  'w-full font-mono rounded-none border border-(--field-border)',
  'h-(--field-control-h) px-3.5',
  'bg-muted text-foreground placeholder:text-foreground/35',
  'transition-[border-color,background-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse',
  // Focus and invalid stay literal, so they outrank the published border and always
  // win — including on a read-only field, which is still focusable and still the
  // field the caret should be able to reach.
  'data-[hovered]:not-data-[focused]:border-(--field-hover)',
  'data-[focused]:outline-none data-[focused]:border-primary',
  'data-[invalid]:not-data-[focused]:border-destructive',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40',
  // Read-only gets the cursor and nothing else that dims it. `opacity` here would
  // take the *value* down with it — at 40% the text measures 3.42:1, under the 4.5:1
  // body text needs, so the one thing the user came to read becomes the thing they
  // cannot.
  'group-data-[readonly]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-hint`: 12px, tighter tracking, white 55%. */
export const HINT = 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-foreground/55'

/**
 * The sheet paints its error state yellow, because the original design had only
 * two accents and yellow was the nearest thing to a warning it owned. That does
 * not carry over here: `--warning` is this system's `secondary` button, so
 * errors would be the same colour as a secondary action. The error state uses
 * `--destructive`, the danger hue, and keeps the sheet's flex so an icon can be
 * dropped in front of the message.
 */
export const ERROR =
  'flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-destructive'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix__unit` and `.ds-affix__icon`: pinned to the control's
 * box, vertically centred, and never a click target — the affix is decoration, and
 * a pointer-events-owning overlay would swallow clicks meant for the field. Sized
 * in `cap` like `Button.Icon`, so one icon works at every field `size`.
 */
export const ICON = [
  'absolute inset-y-0 z-10 grid place-items-center pointer-events-none',
  'text-foreground/70',
  '[&>svg]:block [&>svg]:h-[1.5cap] [&>svg]:w-auto [&>svg]:shrink-0',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet insets both affixes 14px from their edge. */
export const ICON_POSITIONS = {
  start: 'start-3.5',
  end: 'end-3.5',
} as const

export type IconPosition = keyof typeof ICON_POSITIONS

docs:
Text with tokens inside it — a notification target, an alert's audience.

```tsx
<TokenField
  defaultValue={
    new TokenFieldValue([
      { type: 'token', text: '#ops', value: 'ops' },
      { type: 'text', text: ' on call' },
    ])
  }
>
  <TokenField.Label>Notify</TokenField.Label>
  <TokenField.Input />
  <TokenField.Hint>
    Backspace removes the token before the caret.
  </TokenField.Hint>
</TokenField>
```

| Slot               | React Aria   | Notes                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `TokenField`       | `TokenField` | The value is a `TokenFieldValue`, not a set of keys |
| `TokenField.Label` | `Label`      |                                                     |
| `TokenField.Input` | `TokenInput` | The typing surface, and where tokens are drawn      |
| `TokenField.Token` | `Token`      | Only meaningful inside `TokenField.Input`           |
| `TokenField.Hint`  | `Text`       |                                                     |

## A token is part of the value, not a chip beside it

That is the whole difference from `TagGroup`. A tag group is **a set of chips you edit as a set** —
order does not matter, each has an identity, and the control's job is to add and remove them. Here the
tokens are **words inside a sentence the user is writing**, in order, and React Aria puts the caret
between them. `TagGroup` answers _which labels apply_; this answers _who hears about it, and what do
you want to say_.

So the value is a `TokenFieldValue` — a string with tokens embedded — rather than an array of keys, and
`onChange` hands back the whole thing.

## The shape of the segments, which is not what you would guess

`TokenField.Input`'s `children` is a function, and it is called **only for tokens**:

```
case 'token':  →  children(segment)        // wrapped in zero-width spaces
case 'text':   return v.text               // a bare string, never passed to children
```

Two consequences, both of which cost a round here:

- **A text segment is not an element.** There is no node to put a `data-slot` on, and the typing
  surface's own `textContent` _is_ the sentence. So its type and colour belong on
  `TokenField.Input` — a slot for text would be dead code that looks correct in the source.
- **The parameter is typed as a token segment**, so `segment.type === 'token'` is a condition the
  compiler knows is always true. eslint says so directly: _"comparison is always true, since
  `"token" === "token"` is true"_. That lint error is the contract restated.

The zero-width spaces React Aria wraps each token in are for caret placement and are not part of what
the user sees; a test that reads the sentence has to strip them.

## No validation, and so no `Error` slot

React Aria 1.22's token field takes `isDisabled`, `isReadOnly`, `allowsNewlines` and keyboard handlers
— and **no validation props at all**: no `isInvalid`, no `isRequired`, no `validationBehavior`. An
`errorMessage` slot would render and never be wired to anything, which is worse than not having one, so
there is no `TokenField.Error`. This follows the house rule that a component is trimmed rather than
shipped broken.

## No `placeholder` either

A text field's placeholder belongs to its input element, and this container is a `role="textbox"`
`div` with none to put it on. The text content of the value is what stands in for it.

## The keyboard is most of the component

Backspace at a token's edge removes it; the arrow keys step through tokens as single characters; typing
filters what remains. None of that is implemented here, and all of it is the reason to use this rather
than compose a text field with chips.
